messages.subject: Function unite unable to work
parts:
Hello,
 
I am trying to use methylkit for differential analysis and am following the tutorial from the methylkit sight. However, I am receiving the error: 
Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  : unable to find an inherited method for function ‘unite’ for signature ‘"list"’

I have tried changing the object for the function but still arrive at this error for the following code below. Any help would be appreciated! 


######code
files <- list.files(path = wpath, pattern = "\\.bam$", full.names = TRUE)

# Create an empty list to store the processed methylRaw objects
methRaw_list <- list()

# Iterate over each file path and process them individually
for (i in seq_along(files)) {
  # Reading the methylation calls from sorted Bismark alignments
  methRaw <- processBismarkAln(
    location = files[i],  # Specify the current file path
    sample.id = paste0("test", i),  # Generate sample ID dynamically
    assembly = "mm10",
    #save.context = c("CpG", "CHG", "CHH"),
    read.context = "CpG",
    #save.folder = getwd()
  )
  
# unite function from methylKit package
meth <- unite(methRaw_list, destrand=TRUE)


Thanks!

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: Function unite unable to work
parts:
Hi,

The problem that caused unite() to fail was that you gave it a `list` object instead of a `methylRawList`. Using a for-loop to process the single BAM files is fine, as long as the final list will be converted into a methylRawList. 

The recommended way to use multiple files with processBismarkAln would be to pass a list (!) of locations, sample.ids and a treatment vector, directly creating a methylRawList (see examples at the functions help).

Best,
Alex

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: Function unite unable to work
parts:
Also, the purpose of unite() is to merge the methylRaw objects within a methylRawList, thus it does not work with a single methylRaw object. 

Best,
Alex
